title: Affineness from a principal affine part and a closed complementary image
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $V$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $j:V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a quasi-compact immersion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $f\in A$. Suppose $j^{-1}D(f)$ is affine and the subset $j(V)\cap V(f)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then $V$ is affine. Here $D(f)$ is the set of primes not containing $f$ and $V(f)$ its closed complement.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $C=j(V)\cap V(f)$. By the definition of immersion, factor $j$ as a closed immersion $i:V\to W$ followed by the inclusion of an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$. In particular $j(V)\subseteq W$; no assertion about a closed subscheme structure on $C$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0C3A (lemma-get-affine), proof; applied with X = Spec A and U = D(f), as cited at the start of Tag 0ABH (more-groupoids-lemma-get-affine).

proof.text: For $x\in W$, the principal-open basis gives $g\in A$ with $x\in D(g)\subseteq W$. The localization open immersion identifies $D(g)$ with the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$. The closed immersion $i$ is affine, so its inverse image of this affine open of $W$ is affine. This inverse image is exactly $j^{-1}D(g)$.

source.place: Tag 0C3A (lemma-get-affine), proof; applied with X = Spec A and U = D(f), as cited at the start of Tag 0ABH (more-groupoids-lemma-get-affine).

proof.text: The open $D(f)$ is affine by the localization open immersion, and $V_f=j^{-1}D(f)$ is affine by hypothesis. Thus the restricted morphism $j_f:V_f\to D(f)$ is affine, since both schemes are affine. In particular $D(f)$ itself is an affine neighbourhood with affine inverse image for each of its points.

source.place: Tag 0C3A (lemma-get-affine), proof; applied with X = Spec A and U = D(f), as cited at the start of Tag 0ABH (more-groupoids-lemma-get-affine).

proof.text:
Let $x
otin W\cup D(f)$. Since $C\subseteq W$ is closed in $X$, choose a principal neighbourhood $x\in D(g)\subseteq X\setminus C$. A point of $V$ mapping into $D(g)$ cannot map into $V(f)$: otherwise its image would belong to $C\cap D(g)$. Hence $j^{-1}D(g)=j^{-1}(D(g)\cap D(f))$ as open subschemes. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, $fg
otin\mathfrak p$ iff both $f,g
otin\mathfrak p$, so $D(g)\cap D(f)=D(fg)$. The localization open immersion makes $D(fg)$ affine, and it is an open subscheme of $D(f)$. As $j_f$ is affine, its inverse image of $D(fg)$ is affine. Consequently $j^{-1}D(g)$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0C3A (lemma-get-affine), proof; applied with X = Spec A and U = D(f), as cited at the start of Tag 0ABH (more-groupoids-lemma-get-affine).

proof.text: The neighbourhoods in the preceding three cases cover $X$ by affine opens with affine inverse images. Affineness local on the target therefore makes $j$ affine. Applying the definition of affine morphism to the affine open $X$ itself gives $V=j^{-1}(X)$ affine.
